## CAP-13 Presence graph and connection requests

`ditto.presence()` returns `&Arc<Presence>`. The block is generated from a test that CI
compiles and runs on one peer (graph read, observer registration, metadata, handler
installation; the handler itself only fires when a second peer connects):

<!-- snippet: rust-presence -->
<!-- Generated by scripts/sync-snippets.py from code CI runs. Edit the marked source, not this block. -->
```rust
use dittolive_ditto::presence::{ConnectionRequest, ConnectionRequestAuthorization};

fn configure_presence(ditto: &Ditto) -> Result<PresenceObserver, DittoError> {
    // Visible to peers in their graph and in connection requests (4 KiB limit).
    ditto
        .presence()
        .set_peer_metadata(&json!({ "role": "gateway", "app_version": "1.4.0" }))?;

    ditto
        .presence()
        .set_connection_request_handler(|request: ConnectionRequest| {
            // Runs on a Ditto thread with a 10 s deadline: decide without I/O.
            match request
                .peer_metadata()
                .get("app_version")
                .and_then(|v| v.as_str())
            {
                Some(version) if version.starts_with("1.") => ConnectionRequestAuthorization::Allow,
                _ => ConnectionRequestAuthorization::Deny,
            }
        });

    let graph = ditto.presence().graph();
    println!("local peer {}", graph.local_peer.peer_key);
    ditto.presence().register_observer(|graph: &PresenceGraph| {
        println!("{} remote peer(s)", graph.remote_peers.len());
    })
}
```
<!-- /snippet -->

| API | Notes |
|---|---|
| `presence().graph() -> PresenceGraph` | `local_peer: Peer`, `remote_peers: Vec<Peer>` |
| `presence().register_observer(Fn(&PresenceGraph)) -> Result<PresenceObserver>` | call `cancel()` to stop |
| `set_peer_metadata(&impl Serialize)` / `peer_metadata()` | 4 KiB limit; seen by peers |
| `set_connection_request_handler(handler)` / `(None)` | sync handler, 10 s deadline, then deny |
| `set_connection_request_handler_async(handler)` | async; all requests share one current-thread runtime, one at a time |

`Peer` fields include `peer_key`, `device_name`, `os`, `connections`,
`is_connected_to_ditto_server`, `ditto_sdk_version`, `peer_metadata` and
`identity_service_metadata` (`#[non_exhaustive]`). `ConnectionType` is
`#[non_exhaustive]`: match with a `_` arm.

## Rules

- `ConnectionRequestAuthorization::Allow` / `::Deny` are associated constants, not enum
  variants; they still work in `match` arms and returns.
- Decide connection requests from `request.peer_metadata()` and
  `request.identity_service_metadata()` without I/O: a slow handler denies by timeout,
  and with the async form it delays every later request.
- The `Ditto::presence` rustdoc says the observer is cancelled when dropped, but
  `PresenceObserver` has no `Drop` impl (source: `src/presence/observer.rs`). Not
  verified at runtime: call `cancel()`, as for store observers.
- Do not use the presence graph to decide whether data synced; use
  [sync.md](sync.md#cap-14-sync-status-and-local-commit-tracking).
- How the mesh forms and which transports connect peers: `ditto-mesh-networking`, or
  <https://docs.ditto.live/sdk/latest/sync/using-mesh-presence>.
